strategy.summary: openapi.yaml now returns an order's total as `total: { amount, currency }` and adds `POST /orders/{id}/cancel` (200 with the cancelled order, 404 unknown, 409 already cancelled). src/app.js already implements both; test/orders.test.js still asserts `totalCents` (so it fails today) and has no cancel tests. Update that one GET assertion and add cancel tests to the same file, leaving every other test untouched.
inScope: GET /orders/{id} 200 body shape with total {amount, currency}
outOfScope: Products endpoints and the POST /orders tests (AC3: left as they are)
Stock being restored on cancel (not in the spec or ticket)
assumptions: The real app runs in-process (createApp on port 0) as the existing spec does; nothing is faked.
Each test places its own order, so ids come from the response, not from order of execution.
Currency is USD because store.js sets it for every order; amount is priceCents × quantity in cents (Kettle 2499 × 2 = 4998).
Modifying the existing GET-with-total test in place (its title kept) is the 'API tests assert the total as the spec describes'; all other existing tests stay byte-identical.
Cancel tests go in test/orders.test.js, reusing its inline server setup and placeOrder helper, rather than a new file.

risks.description: Total asserted loosely (e.g. any number) would pass if amount were in dollars or currency missing
risks.mitigation: toEqual on the exact body with amount 4998 and currency 'USD'

risks.description: Cancel returns 200 but doesn't persist the cancelled status
risks.mitigation: TC5 reads the order back after cancelling

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /orders/{id} is asserted to return total as { amount (minor units), currency } and no totalCents
POST /orders/{id}/cancel is tested for 200 with the cancelled order, 404 for an unknown order and 409 for an already cancelled order
Other existing API tests are unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.metBy: The diff touches only the totalCents assertion in test/orders.test.js's GET test plus the ticket tag comment and the new cancel describe block; test/products.test.js and the POST /orders tests are unchanged.

testCases.title: returns an order with its total
testCases.expected: 200 and body exactly { id, productId: 1, quantity: 2, status: 'placed', total: { amount: 4998, currency: 'USD' } }
testCases.rationale: The existing test asserts the old totalCents field; update it to the spec's Money shape.

testCases.title: cancels a placed order and returns it
testCases.expected: 200 and body exactly { id, productId: 3, quantity: 1, status: 'cancelled', total: { amount: 699, currency: 'USD' } }
testCases.rationale: Success response of the new operation, shaped as the spec's Order.

testCases.title: shows the order as cancelled once cancelled
testCases.rationale: Proves the cancel persists rather than only being reflected in its response.

testCases.title: is 404 for cancelling an unknown order
is 409 for cancelling an order already cancelled
preconditions: A placed order that has been cancelled once
testCases.expected: Second cancel is 409 with body { error: <string> }

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services; vitest starts the app in-process on an OS-chosen port. Run with `npm test`.
